# What are quality updates

Day 3, 12:00 · Google · coverage: transcript, slides

Why Search changes: feature updates, core updates and spam updates, and what recovery means. The speaker is not named.

- **[Stage]** A drop after a core update can simply mean that a competitor now does better because Google rethought how it assesses quality as a whole.
  <br><sub>`D3-C297` · Day 3, What are quality updates (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Google Search's core updates and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's 'Recoveries' slide advised sites affected by a core update to keep doing a great job, look at what competitors are doing better and learn from sites that are doing better.
  <br><sub>`D3-C298` · Day 3, What are quality updates (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Google Search's core updates and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates), [What site owners should know about Google's August 2019 core update](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2019/08/core-updates)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** After a core update drop, plan a site-wide quality review instead of page-by-page fixes or a technical 'recovery': have someone outside the team assess the site, compare it with the pages that gained, and test whether users can finish their task, for example with short satisfaction surveys.
  <br><sub>`D3-C299` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, What are quality updates · [Google Search's core updates and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/updates/core-updates)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Weight spam audits toward scaled content abuse: a Googler said that type would replace link spam on the slide, so review mass-produced pages, including AI-generated ones, before older link-building patterns.
  <br><sub>`D3-C300` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, What are quality updates · Used by `DEV-SPM-02`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For developers, Google's five listed spam types map to concrete checks: serve Googlebot the same content as users (cloaking), avoid near-identical location or keyword pages (doorways), add value to reused content (scraped content), and patch and monitor the CMS against injected pages and links (hacked content).
  <br><sub>`D3-C301` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, What are quality updates · Used by `DEV-SPM-03`</sub>
